sections.text: # Authoritarian Resurgence in the 21st Century
## The Big Picture

20TH-CENTURY TOTALITARIANISM    vs.    21ST-CENTURY AUTHORITARIANISM
  ┌──────────────────────────────┐        ┌────────────────────────────┐
  │ • Mass mobilization          │        │ • Demobilization:          │
  │   (Nuremberg rallies,        │        │   citizens should be       │
  │   Soviet parades)            │        │   passive, not active      │
  │                              │        │                            │
  │ • Transformative ideology    │        │ • Legitimacy through       │
  │   (utopian goals —           │        │   performance:             │
  │   classless society,         │        │   GDP, security,           │
  │   thousand-year Reich)       │        │   national pride           │
  │                              │        │                            │
  │ • Extreme coercion           │        │ • Selective coercion:      │
  │   (Gulag, Holocaust,         │        │   targeted repression,     │
  │   Cultural Revolution)       │        │   not mass violence        │
  │                              │        │                            │
  │ • Command economy            │        │ • Market integration:      │
  │   (autarky, state            │        │   state capitalism,        │
  │   ownership of everything)   │        │   not autarky              │
  │                              │        │                            │
  │ • International isolation    │        │ • Global integration:      │
  │   or expansion by war        │        │   WTO members, global      │
  │                              │        │   trade, BRI               │
  └──────────────────────────────┘        └────────────────────────────┘
```
## Competitive Authoritarianism
Levitsky and Way (*Competitive Authoritarianism: Hybrid Regimes After the Cold War*, 2010) define:

**Competitive authoritarianism**: Regimes where elections are held and meaningful (they can be lost), but the playing field is systematically tilted in favor of the incumbent through:
- Control of key state resources and media
- Selective harassment of opposition
- Manipulation of electoral rules
- Sporadic but credible use of coercion

DIMENSION          DEMOCRATIC        COMPETITIVE AUTHORITARIAN
  ──────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
  Media access       All parties       State media dominant;
                     can compete       private media
                                       self-censors or captured

Campaign finance   Legal limits      State resources
                     apply to all      available to incumbent

State resources    Neutral civil     Civil servants
                     service           campaign for incumbent

Opposition         Protected by      Selective prosecution
  activity           law               of opposition leaders

Electoral          Independent       Loyalists on commission
  management

Elections          Genuinely         Hold them; occasionally
  themselves         uncertain         rig if needed

KEY: Incumbent doesn't cancel elections; wins them,
       but through structural advantages, not just
       popularity
```
## Russia's Hybrid War Model
Russia under Putin developed a model of political warfare that combines conventional and unconventional tools.
### The Gerasimov Doctrine (Contested)
Valery Gerasimov, Chief of the Russian General Staff, published an article in 2013 (*Military-Industrial Courier*) that was interpreted in the West as describing a doctrine of "non-linear war":

"The role of non-military means of achieving political
  and strategic goals has grown, and, in many cases, they
  have exceeded the power of force of weapons in their
  effectiveness."

TOOLKIT:
  ┌─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┐
  │ • Information operations (disinformation campaigns)     │
  │ • Cyber attacks (Estonia 2007, Georgia 2008)            │
  │ • Political warfare (funding extremist parties in Europe)│
  │ • Economic coercion (gas supply manipulation)           │
  │ • "Little green men" (unmarked forces — Crimea 2014)    │
  │ • Proxies (Donbas 2014 — deniable military support)     │
  │ • Reflexive control theory (shape adversary's decisions │
  │   by managing their information environment)            │
  └─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┘

CAVEAT: Mark Galeotti (who popularized the phrase
  "Gerasimov Doctrine") later acknowledged the doctrine
  was a Western analytical construct, not a Russian
  self-described strategy. Gerasimov was describing
  Western hybrid tactics used in color revolutions.
```
### Russia's Information Operations

Russian information operations (Internet Research Agency, GRU) targeted Western democracies:
- 2016 US election: social media manipulation, DNC hack and leak
- Brexit: RT coverage, possible funding of Leave.eu
- European elections: funding of far-right parties (France's RN, Italy's Lega)
The goal is not necessarily to elect specific candidates but to **amplify polarization and undermine trust in democratic institutions** — making democratic societies doubt their own systems.
## Digital Authoritarianism: China's Model
China has developed the most sophisticated digital authoritarian system in history.
### The Great Firewall

TRAFFIC ENTERING CHINA
          │
          ▼
  ┌────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┐
  │  IP BLOCKING                                           │
  │  Specific IP ranges/addresses blacklisted              │
  │  (Google, Facebook, Twitter, YouTube, Wikipedia)       │
  └────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┘
          │
          ▼
  ┌────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┐
  │  DNS POISONING                                         │
  │  DNS queries for banned domains return wrong IP        │
  │  (or NXDOMAIN)                                         │
  └────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┘
          │
          ▼
  ┌────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┐
  │  DEEP PACKET INSPECTION (DPI)                          │
  │  Content-based filtering; VPN traffic detection        │
  │  (VPN use is technically possible but legally          │
  │   restricted; protocols fingerprinted)                 │
  └────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┘
          │
          ▼
  ┌────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┐
  │  KEYWORD FILTERING                                     │
  │  Real-time content scanning on domestic platforms      │
  │  WeChat, Weibo: automated removal of banned terms      │
  │  "Tiananmen", "Xi Jinping resign", etc.                │
  └────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┘
          │
          ▼
  ┌────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┐
  │  ACCOUNT-LEVEL SURVEILLANCE AND IDENTITY LINKAGE       │
  │  Real-name registration required for all platforms     │
  │  Mobile number → identity → content tracked            │
  └────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┘

RESULT: A parallel Chinese internet (WeChat, Weibo, Baidu,
  Alibaba, ByteDance/Douyin) that is large, functional,
  commercially vibrant, and fully surveilled
```
### Social Credit System
The "social credit system" is often misrepresented in Western media as a single unified score. The reality is more fragmented:

- **Corporate social credit**: Regulatory compliance tracking for businesses — existing compliance systems digitized
- **Financial credit scoring**: Similar to Western credit scores
- **Sectoral blacklists**: Lists of people banned from taking flights or trains for unpaid debts, court judgments — these are the widely reported cases
- **Pilot local programs**: Rongcheng (Shandong) ran a citizen score pilot; it has not been scaled nationally

The unified dystopian score assigning one number to every citizen is not currently deployed at scale. But the infrastructure for pervasive surveillance does exist, and enforcement is real in blacklist programs.
### Technology Export

China exports surveillance technology through:
- **Huawei**: 5G infrastructure with presumed Chinese state access
- **Hikvision, Dahua**: CCTV systems sold globally (70+ countries)
- **ZTE**: Telecom infrastructure
- **CloudWalk**: Face recognition in Zimbabwe
- **Alibaba Cloud**: Data infrastructure
The pattern: BRI financing packages sometimes include surveillance infrastructure. The risk: surveillance architecture that CCP uses domestically can be replicated by purchasing governments.
## Authoritarian Learning and Diffusion
Authoritarian regimes learn from each other, share techniques, and coordinate:

IDEOLOGICAL INSPIRATION:
  Putin → Orbán (illiberal democracy reference)
  Singapore → China (developmental authoritarianism)
  Orbán → PiS Poland, Bolsonaro Brazil

TECHNICAL ASSISTANCE:
  China → Ethiopia, Zimbabwe (surveillance tech)
  Russia → Belarus, Venezuela (political warfare)
  China → Cambodia (internet governance model)

INSTITUTIONAL COOPERATION:
  SCO (Shanghai Cooperation Organisation):
  Counterterrorism cooperation often means sharing
  lists of dissidents and suppressing Uyghurs,
  Tibetans, Falun Gong across borders

ECONOMIC DEPENDENCE:
  BRI recipients become dependent on Chinese finance
  → hesitate to criticize China internationally
  → vote with China in UN

ACADEMIC/ELITE NETWORKS:
  Chinese Communist Party provides training programs
  for ruling parties of allied states
  ("South-South cooperation" framing)
```
## Why Is Authoritarianism "Winning"?

ECONOMIC PERFORMANCE:
  China's sustained growth (9%+ for decades) provides
  authoritarian model with genuine legitimacy.
  "China grew faster than India without democracy."
  Counter: selection bias (also Zimbabwe, Venezuela,
  USSR show authoritarian failure at scale)

DECISION SPEED:
  Authoritarian systems can make rapid decisions
  (infrastructure, industrial policy) without
  democratic veto points.
  Counter: rapid bad decisions (Mao's Great Leap Forward)

INFORMATION CONTROL:
  Can shape domestic perception of performance;
  disadvantages independent media
  → regime can maintain popularity through
  managed information environment

DEMOCRATIC DISILLUSIONMENT:
  Western democracies' failures (2008 crisis,
  Iraq War, COVID response in US/UK)
  discredited the model
  → authoritarianism benefits from comparison
```
## Democratic Resilience Factors

```
WHY SOME DEMOCRACIES SURVIVE AUTHORITARIAN PRESSURE
════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════

DOMESTIC:
  ┌──────────────────────────────────────────────────┐
  │ Strong civil society: unions, churches, NGOs     │
  │ Independent judiciary with strong tradition      │
  │ Robust opposition parties                        │
  │ Economically independent private media           │
  │ Federal structure (state govts as resistance)    │
  │ Civic culture of democratic norms                │
  └──────────────────────────────────────────────────┘

INTERNATIONAL:
  ┌──────────────────────────────────────────────────┐
  │ EU membership (conditionality, funding leverage) │
  │ NATO membership (at least marginal military      │
  │  independence from Russia)                       │
  │ US support for democratic opposition             │
  │ International media attention                    │
  └──────────────────────────────────────────────────┘

HISTORICAL:
  ┌──────────────────────────────────────────────────┐
  │ Prior democratic experience matters              │
  │ Czech Republic more resilient than Hungary —     │
  │  richer civic tradition, Havel legacy            │
  │ Baltic states more resistant to Russian pressure │
  │  — memory of Soviet occupation is recent         │
  └──────────────────────────────────────────────────┘
```

## Decision Cheat Sheet

| If you need to diagnose... | Start With | Key Caveat |
|---|---|---|
| 21st-century authoritarianism | Demobilization, performance legitimacy, selective coercion, market integration | Do not map it mechanically onto 20th-century totalitarian mobilization. |
| Competitive authoritarian regimes | Levitsky-Way: real elections tilted by media, resources, and selective harassment | Elections may be loseable in theory while systematically unfair in practice. |
| China's censorship architecture | IP blocking, DNS poisoning, DPI, keyword filtering, real-name identity linkage | The Great Firewall is layered infrastructure, not a single switch. |
| Social credit claims | Fragmented blacklists, corporate compliance systems, and local pilots | A unified national citizen score is mostly a Western misunderstanding so far. |
| Authoritarian diffusion | Ideological inspiration, technical assistance, institutional cooperation, dependence | Diffusion is not command-and-control; regimes adapt borrowed tools locally. |
| Russian information operations | Polarization, institutional distrust, and amplification of existing divisions | The goal is often demoralization and doubt, not belief conversion. |
